subject.title: [Google Antigravity Ban] Frequent Tool Schema Reloading Causes False Positive Anti-Abuse Detection

question: Should OpenClaw land a bounded internal cache for provider-normalized tool schema parameters now, or defer this issue to the broader prepared-runtime migration?
rationale: The repeated-normalization path is source-proven, but the permanent cache boundary affects provider hooks, plugin metadata lifecycle, custom provider behavior, and the prepared-runtime rollout direction.

options.title: Land narrow internal cache
options.body: Refresh or replace the open cache PR so only known safe bundled normalizers cache cloned schema parameters while fresh tool objects, closures, and custom hooks remain per-turn.

options.title: Defer to prepared runtime
options.body: Keep this issue open until the prepared-runtime migration carries enough provider/tool facts to remove the need for a separate cache layer.

options.title: Require live repro first
options.body: Hold implementation until a maintainer or reporter captures current-main live Google/Gemini or heap proof that the user-visible impact still occurs.

recommendation.title: Land narrow internal cache
recommendation.body: Refresh or replace the open cache PR so only known safe bundled normalizers cache cloned schema parameters while fresh tool objects, closures, and custom hooks remain per-turn.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice intersects the prepared-runtime migration and request-time rediscovery boundary this owner has been carrying.
